lines.text: We had invited every lord north of the Senn. Eleven of them. Pell said it was the first Moot the north had called in a hundred years.
Writing letters is cheap, my lord. Lords don't come to a zero's hall. They'll send another polite letter, saying they've caught a cold.
Eight lords sent polite letters. Three of them really had caught colds. And three lords came.
The first came on the biggest horse I had ever seen. Even so, his feet nearly touched the ground.
So you're the boy who makes the north warm! You're older than they told me.
That's the lord, Lord Kesting. Down there.
That? I've had breakfasts bigger than that.
Welcome to Greyhollow, Lord Kesting. We'll find you a bigger breakfast.
Ilse shook everyone's hand, as usual. She still called it a southern custom.
Rime. Five rings, every one of them his own. He has held Kesting Pass against the Pale for forty years.
Lady Ysolde Marrick. I brought my own bread, Lord Lucan. I hear yours is too good to be true.
Iron. Three rings. The cleverest lord in the north, and the poorest. Her husband died owing money to everyone, including Kesting.
Lord Penhallow. Five rings, since you're wondering. Everyone always is.
His father was a three. His grandfather was a three. Then at twenty-nine, the boy woke up a five.
Discipline, Kesting. You should try it.
Rings don't grow after sixteen. Everyone knows that. Everyone except Greyhollow. So how had his?
Five. But it feels wrong. Like a candle burning in someone else's lantern.
Ash didn't growl at people. He growled at Penhallow.
Can I shoot that one?
Not yet.
Three lords, in a zero's hall. Bram didn't say a word all evening. He just polished the same cup for an hour.
And that night, Lord Penhallow stood at his window for a long time, looking across the yard. At the keep. At Ilse's window.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter forty-nine, coming soon.
